overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is a public administrative body responsible for adjudicating petitions for variances, special permits, and Chapter 40B comprehensive permits, as well as hearing administrative appeals of municipal building violations. Operating across a meeting record spanning from April 6, 2023, to September 24, 2026, the board evaluates dimensional, use, site plan, and environmental conditions for residential and commercial properties throughout Medford. Over this period, the board has processed major multi-family M.G.L. Chapter 40B housing developments, commercial site expansions, auto and cannabis business permits, and residential nonconformity extensions. At its most recent meeting, the board evaluated residential use variances and commercial special permits while continuing applications for accessory dwelling units to review modified designs and obtain guidance on state zoning regulations.

threads.name: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway Chapter 40B Permit
threads.summary: The board opened hearings in April 2023 to evaluate a M.G.L. Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application for a proposed 350-unit, eight-story residential development at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway. Deliberations focused on peer reviews for stormwater management, site congestion, fire safety, linkage fee exemptions, and bicycle storage restrictions. In July 2023, the board approved the comprehensive permit with conditions covering phased occupancy, public art, and a partial linkage fee waiver for market-rate units. The project returned to the board in October 2024, when members determined that design refinements to trash rooms, bike storage, and rooftop amenities constituted insubstantial changes under 40B regulations.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B Permit
threads.summary: In November 2023, the board began reviewing a Chapter 40B application for a proposed 289-unit multi-family development at 970 Fellsway and authorized hiring peer review consultants. Through early 2024, the board and peer reviewers conducted detailed sessions addressing site massing, traffic impact assessments, civil engineering, stormwater management, and local regulatory waivers. The board voted to approve the comprehensive permit in May 2024, granting a partial linkage fee waiver based on proposed off-site public improvements and settling final peer review and transit conditions. In January 2025, the board granted a special permit to allow a partial commercial building demolition and lot split to preserve lot coverage requirements alongside the approved residential project.

threads.name: 280 Mystic Avenue Chapter 40B Permit
threads.summary: The board initiated review of a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application for a 378-unit residential development at 280 Mystic Avenue in April 2024, authorizing peer review consultants and staff working sessions. In May 2024, the board voted to require the applicant to pay peer review fees by a specified deadline due to a lack of responsiveness. In June 2024, the board accepted the applicant's formal request to withdraw the comprehensive permit petition.

threads.name: Cannabis Special Permits at 114 Mystic Avenue
threads.summary: In April 2023, the board approved a special permit for New England Organics LLC to operate a retail marijuana dispensary at 114 Mystic Avenue with conditions for traffic safety and signage placement. In May 2026, the board granted special permits to Victory Gardens for medical cannabis sales and product manufacturing at the same location, while continuing an application for courier delivery services. After further continuances awaiting legal counsel, the board approved the special permit allowing cannabis delivery services in July 2026.

threads.name: Board Leadership and Administrative Rules
threads.summary: In April 2023, the board voted to move its regular meeting start time from 7:30 PM to 6:30 PM beginning in May 2023. In April 2024, the board elected Jamie Thompson as chair following the resignation of Mike Caldera. The board initiated discussions in July 2024 regarding the appointment of a subcommittee to update its rules and regulations. Following the resignation of Jamie Thompson, the board elected Mike Caldera as chair in February 2025, while continuing efforts to update administrative procedures and draft outstanding meeting minutes.

citations.title: Administrative Updates and Rules of Order
citations.label: M04#7

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Units and State Zoning Compliance
threads.summary: In July 2026, the board approved a rear yard setback variance for an attached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) at 621 Fulton Street, while continuing companion attic expansion and ADU applications for 1-3 Vassar Street and 12 Wellesley Street to allow legal counsel review under new state zoning regulations. The Vassar Street and Wellesley Street applications were continued through August 2026 to maintain voting member consistency. In September 2026, the board continued both petitions to October 2026 to allow the applicant to present smaller modified designs and to obtain additional legal counsel regarding state ADU rules.

threads.name: Commercial and Auto Business Permitting
threads.summary: The board evaluated multiple petitions for commercial expansions and vehicle services across several sessions. In March 2024 and April 2024, the board reviewed a petition for 38 Harvard Avenue, ultimately approving a use variance for limited Class 2 used motor vehicle sales at an existing repair shop subject to screening conditions. In May 2024, the board approved an amendment to a height variance at 400 Mystic Avenue to allow the construction of a new service facility and car elevator for an auto dealership. The board later granted a six-month variance extension for the vehicle sales use at 38 Harvard Avenue in June 2025.

periods.narrative: The board reviewed residential variances, commercial permits, and initiated extensive Chapter 40B comprehensive permit reviews for major multi-family housing projects.
The board processed multiple Chapter 40B applications, adjusted internal board leadership, and granted dimensional and use variances for various residential and commercial properties.
The board adjudicated business violation appeals, commercial special permits, and began evaluating accessory dwelling unit proposals in relation to state zoning rules.
